clue.text: American state allowance R for a gypsy

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
a grant is a sum of money allowed to someone

explanation.surface: A US state hands out a benefit payment to a traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A gypsy in the old loose sense is a wanderer with no fixed home, which is a vagrant.

clue.text: Speak of the old devil over the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed over the next comes first

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, an old name for the devil
a course is a route or way

explanation.surface: Talk about the devil, who lives across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourse is to talk at length on a subject, so it means to speak.

clue.text: Sound cold food additive

indicators.note: Sound says the word meaning cold is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: chilly means cold

explanation.surface: A healthy, chilled ingredient added to food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli pepper is a hot spice put into dishes, a seasoning added to food.

clue.text: Traffic force cut by two thousand

indicators.note: cut by says the word for force is split open and the thousands go in

parts.note: to coerce is to force
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: A police force has its numbers slashed by two thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in its trading sense means buying and selling, i.e. commerce.

clue.text: Work at home-given wrong coding, yet trust a A settlement can be made

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are set out in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A homeworker is told that despite faulty code a settlement will be reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges CODING, YET, TRUST and A; the closing words are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage industry is small-scale manufacturing done by people in their own houses.

clue.text: Naturally there's no illumination at night

definitions.text: Naturally there's no illumination at night

parts.words: Naturally there's no illumination at night
parts.note: read as natural light: a night when the satellite in the sky gives none of its glow

explanation.definitionFit: A night without the satellite showing is dark by nature, with no natural lamp overhead.

clue.text: Stand taken by a painter

parts.note: not a stance or opinion an artist adopts but the wooden frame that holds the canvas

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's canvas rests on a wooden three-legged frame while being worked on.

clue.text: Get firm with a trainee following dismissal

indicators.note: following places the remaining pieces after the word for dismissal

parts.note: a conge is a formal dismissal, from the French
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: An employer gets tough, taking on an apprentice after sacking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to set or thicken from liquid into a solid state.

clue.text: Drive away when outlaw is given his head

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban

indicators.note: his head means only the leading letter of the word his is wanted

explanation.surface: An outlaw is sent packing once given free rein.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to expel them, sending them off.

clue.text: A great number will get awkward and shout

indicators.note: awkward suggests the words and plus shout are clumsily jumbled up

explanation.surface: A big crowd will turn rowdy and start yelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure in the thousands is a large count.

clue.text: Ornament a couple with a certain constraint

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
a let is a hindrance, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A pair of lovers comes with ties that bind them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a decorative band worn on the wrist, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Being left no money, went before rested

parts.note: O, like zero, stands for nothing
L is the old abbreviation for pounds, from Latin librae
to lead is to go in front, so led

explanation.surface: Someone left penniless had gone ahead and taken a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge or lie about lazily, so lolled means lay idly.

clue.text: Lasting suffering

explanation.surface: Something that persists brings prolonged pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting means durable or permanent; suffering means bearing hardship, putting up with it.

clue.text: See about a flowering plant from the Orient

indicators.note: about says the bishop's seat goes round the flower

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Look at a bloom imported from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is the crossword's usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly wind or course comes out of the east, from the direction of Asia.

clue.text: Showing "sense, rage wildly in enthusiasm

indicators.note: wildly says the words sense and rage are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Showing good judgement while raging furiously out of zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness and zest are what eagerness means: avid, impatient interest.

clue.text: The French assume it to blame, it's learned

indicators.note: assume means take on, so the French article takes the word it inside

parts.note: le is the French masculine article meaning the
taken as written
to rate is to scold or reprove

explanation.surface: The French take the blame, which is a clever thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educated who can read and write well is well read.

clue.text: Dreadfully vain earl made emperor

indicators.note: Dreadfully signals that vain earl is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A conceited nobleman is raised to the imperial throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Valerian was a Roman emperor of the third century.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerian ruled Rome in the 250s before being captured by the Persians.

clue.text: A writer can arrange credit

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: An author can arrange to receive acknowledgement.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to someone is to attribute it to them.

clue.text: Coming to terms in church

indicators.note: Coming to suggests the words terms and in arrive at a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Reaching agreement inside a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, such as York's cathedral.

clue.text: Call for retirement after sitting on food

indicators.note: after places the reversed summons behind the assembly

parts.note: a diet is a formal assembly or session, as of a parliament

indicators.note: retirement suggests drawing back, so the word for call is read from its end

parts.note: to cite is to summon, as to court

explanation.surface: A summons to stand down comes while the committee is debating food.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietetic means relating to diet and nutrition, so concerned with what is eaten.

clue.text: The team numbered one by one

explanation.surface: A side is counted off player by player.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has that many players; written as figures, a one beside a one gives the number.

clue.text: Plan setting many on edge in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in says the pieces sit inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: SE, the South East, is where England's Home Counties lie around London

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another sits next to it, here in front

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A plot puts lots of people on edge in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, so SE (South East).
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a plan or plot to achieve something.

clue.text: Not all of the victims appear put out

indicators.note: Not all of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only some of those harmed seem annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'appear put out' as the definition, but 'appear' does not swap for the answer; it is a link, and 'put out' (expelled) is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict tenants is to expel them from their home.

clue.text: A good man with a bird a good man, but most strict

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good man
an erne is a sea eagle
ST again, the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A virtuous man with a bird, and another virtuous man, though the harshest of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternest is the superlative of stern, harsh or severe.

clue.text: Missing revolutionary isn't holding a Liberal back!

indicators.note: holding says the rearranged word wraps round the reversed pieces
revolutionary says the letters of isn't are turned around into a new order
back means a and the abbreviation for Liberal are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A radical who went missing won't support a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' poses as a noun for a radical, but it is the anagram signal, making SINT; 'back' gives BILA for the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibilant sound is a hissing one, such as s or sh.

clue.text: Resulted from petition presented in extremity

indicators.note: presented in says the word for petition is put inside the word for extremity

parts.note: an end is an extremity
to sue is to petition or appeal, as in sue for peace

explanation.surface: Something came out of a plea made in desperate circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means followed on as a consequence, came about afterwards.

clue.text: Grass by the tracks is anything but tender

parts.note: a lea is a grassy meadow
taken as written
RY is short for railway, the tracks

explanation.surface: Grass growing beside the railway line is tough stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is leathery is tough and chewy, the opposite of soft.
